hook: Michael Kratsios directs the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy in the second Trump administration, after previously serving as US Chief Technology Officer from 2019 to 2021.
name: Michael Kratsios

quote.text: Last July, the Trump administration released Winning the AI Race: America's AI Action Plan, outlining a strategy to maintain global leadership in AI.

moniker: Director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy

reading.body:
Michael Kratsios, confirmed as OSTP Director in March 2025, leads federal coordination of US AI policy across agencies and sets the frame for infrastructure constraints on AI capability development.

Kratsios returns to federal technology leadership after a break of four years, bringing continuity in a role that spans both Trump administrations. His confirmation by a 74-25 Senate vote suggests substantial bipartisan support for his appointment, unusual for technology policy positions. The OSTP directorship places him at the center of federal decisions about research funding, regulatory approach, and interagency technology strategy. His January 2026 testimony referenced the Trump administration's published AI Action Plan, indicating formal doctrine on AI strategy exists as input to his office's work.

The OSTP role does not inherently control the grid, power generation, or building permits that constrain physical AI infrastructure. It shapes policy environment and federal R&D priorities, which are downstream of those physical constraints rather than upstream of them. This matters for AI scaling because policy can accelerate or delay infrastructure deployment, alter public utility regulation, or redirect federal resources toward power and facilities. Kratsios's position influences which constraints receive policy attention, but the office itself does not build data centers or power plants.

quick_facts: Confirmed by the Senate as Director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy on March 25, 2025 by a vote of 74-25
Sworn in as OSTP Director on March 28, 2025 by Vice President JD Vance
Served in an acting capacity as OSTP lead from January 20, 2025 until Senate confirmation
Previously served as US Chief Technology Officer from August 2, 2019 to January 20, 2021, after serving in an acting capacity from January 2017
13th Director of the Office of Science and Technology Policy
